functions.name: readSkeletonData_transformTimelines
functions.address_range: 0x28dca8-0x28de74 (B12, 460 B / 115 insns; the whole transform family, including the scan and the frame loop, is one contiguous block)

abi.signature: int readSkeletonData_transformTimelines(Json* transformMap, void* data_raw, void* animation_raw)
abi.transformMap: the "transform" JSON child. Parent B3 caches the eight root members and stores this one at [sp+0x38] (0x28d35c); B12 loads it at 0x28dca8 and reloads it at 0x28dcb4.
abi.animation_raw: spAnimation* (parent r11; the tail reads +0x04 duration, +0x08 timelineCount, +0x0c timelines)
abi.return: always 1: every exit (0x28dcb0, 0x28dcc0 and the 0x28de70 fall-through) lands on the path block B13 at 0x28de74. There is no error path in this family.

functions.semantics: transformMap == NULL -> 0x28de74 (0x28dca8 ldr / 0x28dcb0 beq). Otherwise constraintNode = transformMap->child (0x28dcb8); NULL -> 0x28de74 (0x28dcc0 beq). Then the five key literals are materialised once outside the loop (0x28dcc4..0x28dcfc: [sp+0x2c] = "time", [sp+0x30] = "rotateMix", [sp+0x34] = "translateMix", [sp+0x38] = "scaleMix", [sp+0x3c] = "shearMix"; the last store overwrites the transformMap slot after its final read). Per constraint node (head 0x28dd00, back edge 0x28de70): name = node->name@+0x1c (0x28dd00), transform = spSkeletonData_findTransformConstraint(data, name) (0x28dd08, result moved to r4 at 0x28dd0c and NEVER null-tested), timeline = spTransformConstraintTimeline_create(node->unk_0c) (0x28dd10/0x28dd14), then the index scan (readSkeletonData_transformConstraintIndex, 0x28dd1c..0x28dd68) and the frame loop (readSkeletonData_transformTimelineFrames, 0x28dd68..0x28de24), then the tail: animation->timelineCount++ with timelines[count] = timeline (0x28de3c..0x28de48), next = node->next (0x28de50), last = frames[(declared-1)*5] (0x28de38/0x28de44/0x28de58), animation->duration = max(duration, last) (0x28de5c..0x28de6c), loop while next != NULL (0x28de68/0x28de70).

field_offsets.spTransformConstraintTimeline.frameFloat: +0x0c = frameCount*5 (0x282a60 mul r0,r7,r5 with r7=5; 0x282a70 str)
field_offsets.spTransformConstraintTimeline.frames: +0x10, five floats per frame (0x28de4c; setFrame body 0x282fd4)
field_offsets.spTransformConstraintTimeline.constraint: +0x14; the only writer in this family is 0x28dd64 (word 0xe5863014, identical to the ik family's 0x28dbcc)

setframe_abi.signature: void spTransformConstraintTimeline_setFrame(void* timeline, int frameIndex, float time, float rotateMix, float translateMix, float scaleMix, float shearMix)
setframe_abi.store_order: 0x282fd0 add r1,r1,r1,lsl#2 (i*5); 0x282fd4 ldr r0,[r0,#0x10] (frames); 0x282fd8 add r12,r1,#1; 0x282fe0 add r1,r0,r1,lsl#2 (&frames[i*5]); 0x282ff4 str r2,[r1] (time); 0x283000 str r3,[r0] (rotateMix); 0x282ff8 str r5,[r0,#4] (translateMix); 0x282ffc str r4,[r0,#8] (scaleMix); 0x283004 str r12,[r0,#0xc] (shearMix)

tail.frame_stride: 5 floats: create 0x282fc0 mov r2,#5; setFrame 0x282fd0 add r1,r1,r1,lsl#2; tail 0x28de38 sub r2,r2,#1 + 0x28de44 add r2,r2,r2,lsl#2 + 0x28de54 add r3,r3,r2,lsl#2
tail.order: the next-pointer load (0x28de50) sits between the frames load (0x28de4c) and the duration compare (0x28de5c); the next-pointer test (0x28de68) comes AFTER the duration store (0x28de6c), so the store is unconditional on the last iteration
tail.declared_wrap: (declared-1) is computed in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic, so declared == 0 wraps to 0xffffffff*5; the original would index far outside the frames array

quirks: No NULL test on the findTransformConstraint result: 0x28dd0c mov r4,r0 is followed directly by 0x28dd10 ldr r0,[r5,#0xc] and the create call.

No error branch exists anywhere in B12 - no _spSkeletonJson_setError call site and no spAnimation_dispose/spSkeletonData_dispose call site, which is why the whole family is 460 bytes with a single exit to 0x28de74.
The frame loop follows the child list (0x28dd7c head, 0x28de20 back edge on r4 != NULL), not the declared count from Json+0x0c; only the create call and the duration index use the declared count.
The transform node loop follows transform->child / node->next, so a "transform" object with a single child runs the whole scan+frames+tail exactly once.

r5 is reused as the translateMix scratch register inside the frame loop (0x28ddc0 mov r5,r0), so the constraint node survives in r12 ([sp+0x14] spill at 0x28dd88, reload 0x28de18, restore 0x28de24). A no-frames node never executes movne r12,r5 and reaches the tail with r5 still the node.
All five key reads happen every frame (no key-presence test): an absent key yields the Json_getFloat default, which is 0.0f for time and 1.0f for the four mix keys.

functions.name: readSkeletonData_transformConstraintIndex
functions.address_range: 0x28dd1c-0x28dd68 (scan; the hit store 0x28dd64 is in-line, unlike the ik family's out-of-line island 0x28dbc8/0x28dbcc)

abi.signature: int readSkeletonData_transformConstraintIndex(void* data_raw, void* transform_raw, void* timeline_raw)
abi.return: reconstruction artefact only: 1 = wrote +0x14, 0 = fell through without writing. Both original exits go to 0x28dd68 and the driver ignores it.

instruction_walk: 0x28dd20 ldr r1,[r0,#0x44]  count snapshot (read once, never re-read)
0x28dd24 cmp r1,#0 ; 0x28dd28 ble 0x28dd68  SIGNED count <= 0 skips the scan and never reads +0x48
0x28dd30 ldr r3,[r2]        element 0 (r3 is reused as the element register)
0x28dd40 b 0x28dd60         element-0 hit -> clear r3 -> store
0x28dd44 ldr r0,[r2,#0x4]!  pre-index writeback: r2 += 4, element re-read from memory
0x28dd48 cmp r4,r0 ; 0x28dd4c beq 0x28dd64  hit at index r3
0x28dd50 add r3,r3,#1 ; 0x28dd54 cmp r3,r1 ; 0x28dd58 bne 0x28dd44  equality against the snapshot, not blt
consequences: A hit at element 0 stores 0; a hit at element i stores i.
A miss stores nothing: +0x14 keeps the create-time value (calloc zero in the original; SENTINEL in the fixture).
count <= 0 (including negative) skips the scan; the +0x48 array word is never read, so it may be NULL.
A NULL lookup result compares equal to a NULL vector slot; otherwise it simply misses.

functions.name: readSkeletonData_transformTimelineFrames

abi.constraintNode: the per-constraint JSON node whose +0x1c is the member key and whose +0x0c is the declared frame count; its child list holds the frame objects

argument_registers.translateMix: r5 (0x28ddc0 mov r5,r0; r5 was the constraint node, preserved in r12)
argument_registers.shearMix: r0 passed straight to the stack slot at 0x28ddf4

functions.frame_index: r7 starts at 0 only when the child list is non-empty (0x28dd70 movne r7,#0) and is incremented after readCurve (0x28de14 add r7,r7,#1)
functions.readcurve_call: 0x28de00 mov r0,r4 (frame) ; 0x28de04 mov r2,r7 (frameIndex) ; 0x28de08 mov r1,r6 (timeline) ; 0x28de0c bl 0x28b34c

differences_vs_ik_precedent: Frame stride is 5 floats per frame (time + four mix keys), not 3: create 0x282fc0 mov r2,#5 and tail 0x28de44 add r2,r2,r2,lsl#2.

The +0x14 hit store is in-line at 0x28dd64 and shares its word (0xe5863014) with the ik store 0x28dbcc, but transform's index-0 clear sits at 0x28dd60 immediately before the store instead of in a separate out-of-line island.
The scan reads count from +0x44 and the array from +0x48 (ik: +0x3c/+0x40).
setFrame takes seven arguments (three on the stack: translateMix, scaleMix, shearMix); ik's takes five (one stack word).
The frame loop needs r12/[sp+0x14] to preserve the constraint node because r5 is reused as the translateMix scratch register; ik's frame loop used r5 for its frame pointer and r4 for the node.
No error path: B12 contains no setError/dispose call site, matching the census statement that the segment has no "Transform constraint not found" literal.
